hook: As an engineering manager, when I came across a resume from a Stanford grad, I would read it a little more closely. That's it.
I've spoken with over 500 developers in the last 12 months. I won't be doing any more 15 minute chats.
In this case AI stood for Actually, Indians.
These are 2 takes on the software job market that I absolutely can't stand:
I once worked at a coding bootcamp where a student didn't know how to open his file explorer.
Junior developers are inherently risky (in every industry, not just tech btw).
He created a full stack app that worked pretty well. It even looked nice. But when I asked how it worked... Oof.
A look back at software engineering in 2024 (according to social media):
At first people laughed. Now, I'm more convinced this is true.
2 things: Are CEOs of large companies really begging their eng department for... anything?
Here's why your company is (probably) struggling to find good developers.
CEOs want to believe the myth of AI.
Breaking into software as: an 18 year old, a 25 year old with no money, a 30 year old with kids.
New coders are obsessed with going to Google, Meta, Amazon or Netflix. These make up a solid .6% of software engineering roles.
As usual, software developers greatly underestimate their own skill while greatly OVER-estimating everyone else.
